messages:
Alex Chen: heads-up — canary run shows ~2.3x host CPU on ingress compared to baseline. client qps identical. suspecting parsing + small-write syscalls. flame looks like most time in header/parsing and writev fallback to single write.
Priya Patel: ugh. any flame output or perf samples? quick paste helps. :eyes:
Alex Chen: pasted flame snippet below from perf script (top stacks trimmed):
```
samples: 12000  cycles:u
  parse_headers  42%  host_io  18%  writev_emulate_single  16%  slab_alloc 9%  tokenize 7%  other 8%
  stack: ingress::parse -> ingress::frame_unwrap -> http::header_scan -> writev_fallback -> syscall(write)
```
Jamie Rivera: can we confirm it's writev falling back or our shim doing small buffers? last week I saw the shim create many 64B buffers instead of one big iovec.
Ryan O'Neill: kernel selection note: I looked at the canary log — model runtime reports a kernel fallback path for short sequences when socket reads are fragmented. If batches arrive as tiny fragments we pick the smaller-gemm kernel which is suboptimal on GPU because it increases host serialization.
Lina Gomez: that matches. fragmentation -> many tiny host parses -> write syscalls -> smaller kernel choices -> worse batching efficiency. multi-hop regression.
Priya Patel: quick triage: can we 1) capture tcpdump for a few minutes 2) enable writev coalesce in host proxy 3) log kernel-selection reasons with sample ids?
Alex Chen: started tcpdump capture (saved to s3). also added extra logging for kernel selection (see log excerpt):
```
[2026-03-20T14:05:12Z] kernel_select: seq_len=48 batch_count=3 chosen=scalar_small reason=fragmented_ingress
[2026-03-20T14:05:13Z] kernel_select: seq_len=512 batch_count=1 chosen=vectorized reason=good_pad
```
Jamie Rivera: I have a microbench for writev coalescing — runs locally and shows 3x fewer syscalls for 10k requests/sec of 8KB frames. quick script:
```
# bench_writev.sh
for n in 10000; do
  ./client --burst=$n --frame=8192 --coalesce=on
done
```
Ryan O'Neill: also parking a thought: batching heuristics currently use a fixed token-window multiplier (x1.5) for short sequences. If fragmentation is high, we should bias towards time-window instead of count-window to allow coalescing in host. i can prototype a time-first policy.
Lina Gomez: +1. also we should try KV cache prefetch hints — when early tokens indicate a high-prob next-block we prefetch relevant cache shards to avoid extra network calls inside the kernel path. might lower tail latency spikes.
Priya Patel: are we sure KV is involved? flame had slab_alloc and kvcache spikes at ~9%. could be allocation churn. perhaps small allocations from header parsing trigger slab pressure which makes kvcache allocations slower.
Alex Chen: yep slab_alloc correlates with parse allocations. i profiled allocations with jemalloc stats; parse path allocates ~200 bytes per header token, amplified by fragmentation.
Jamie Rivera: possible quick wins: 1) coalesce iovecs in host proxy 2) reuse header buffers (thread-local arena) 3) tune batching to favor time-window for short seqs 4) add kernel_select telemetry to rollout.
ingress-bot: deploy canary 5712349000 started by ci-bot — image: ingress-proxy:v3.2.4-coalesce (notes: writev-coalesce enabled).
Alex Chen: rolled v3.2.4 to 10% canary. initial metrics: syscalls/sec down 62%, host CPU down 28% after 5m, but avg latency up 2ms (still investigating).
Ryan O'Neill: latency bump might be due to time-windowing — we'll need to tune window timers. how long is coalesce wait?
Jamie Rivera: current coalesce wait is 1ms. we can try 250us to hit lower latency but still coalesce. I'll run bench combos (250us, 500us, 1ms) and post results.
Priya Patel: action items:
- Jamie: bench coalesce at 250/500/1000us and send numbers (deadline EOD)
- Ryan: prototype time-first batching policy and a small experiment flag (deadline tomorrow)
- Lina: sketch KV prefetch heuristic and estimate ops cost (deadline EOD)
- Alex: collect full perf + jemalloc flame for 30m canary and upload (in progress)
Alex Chen: adding logs to the rollout for kernel_select reasons and seq alignment. i'll post the perf tarball when done. :thumbsup:
Priya Patel: thanks team — this looks actionable. we'll reconvene after benches. :rocket:
